Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. data.cultural_impact: Nokul is a rare and significant Hindu name, rooted in rich cultural history. The name Nokul is believed to be derived from Lord Shiva's weapon, the trident, also known as the Trishula. Shiva, one of the primary deities in Hinduism, is known for his role as the destroyer of evil and chaos, which he achieves through the power of his trident. The trident represents the three fundamental aspects of existence – creation, preservation, and destruction. Thus, the name Nokul carries the powerful symbolism of Lord Shiva and his magical weapon, deeply ingrained in Hindu mythology.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nokul holds significant spiritual significance for those who bear it. It is a constant reminder of the divine power that lies within each individual, echoing Lord Shiva's role as a destroyer of negative energies and igniter of positive change. Furthermore, the name encourages one to harness their inner strength and courage, much like the destructive power of the trident. Overall, Nokul serves as a spiritual anchor, connecting the bearer with the depth and breadth of the Hindu mythological tradition, instilling a sense of purpose, resilience, and determination.

historical_references.reference: Nokul was a legendary king of the Vishwamitra gotra in ancient India. He is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an Indian epic poem.
Nokul is also known as Nagnajit, the slayer of Nagas. He is mentioned in the Puranas, a collection of Hindu scriptures.
